title: Isolation of exophers from cardiomyocyte-reporter mouse strains by fluorescence-activated cell sorting
protocol: Euthanize mouse using CO2 asphyxiation or an institutionally accepted euthanasia procedure.
Place mouse in a supine position on the dissection stage.
Immobilize the mouse by pinning its paws and feet to the stage.
Spray the mouse torso with 70% ethanol.
Make an incision of superficial abdominal tissue below the lower costal bone and diaphragm using forceps and scissors.
Cut upwards toward the head to remove skin, revealing the peritoneal cavity.
Remove the peritoneum to access the peritoneal cavity.
Gently cut the diaphragm laterally while holding the sternum with forceps to access the thoracic cavity and heart.
Cut the two lateral margins of the anterior thorax toward the head and flip it upwards.
Immobilize the anterior thorax by pinning it with a syringe needle to the dissection surface.
Nick the right atrium using surgical scissors.
Hold the heart with the apex pointing upwards using forceps.
Carefully insert a syringe needle into the apex of the heart into the left ventricle.
Inject 10 mL of cold PBS at a flow rate of approximately 5 mL/min for 2 min.
Use a syringe with a 21G needle manually.
Place the needle gently in the left ventricle to avoid puncturing the interventricular septum, pulmonary valves, or atrial valves.
Monitor perfusion effectiveness by observing color changes in liver and lungs.
Perform perfusion within less than 5 minutes after euthanasia to prevent blood coagulation.
Remove the heart carefully by cutting major vessels below the atria.
Trim away left atria to ensure only intact myocardium is isolated.
Carefully remove vessels and atria from the heart in a petri dish with cold PBS.
Place the isolated heart in a 15 mL Falcon tube filled with 3–5 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Place the tube on ice.
Isolate any other desired tissues if needed.
Prepare a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube with 1 mL digestion buffer for each heart.
Put the isolated hearts in the tubes with digestion buffer and mince them into small pieces using surgical scissors.
Place the tubes in a 37°C heat block for 45 minutes with agitation at 100 rpm.
Mix the digestion mixture by gently pipetting up and down using a trimmed 1 mL pipette tip.
Pre-wet a 40 μm strainer placed in a 50 mL Falcon tube with 1 mL sorting buffer.
Transfer the digestion mixture to the strainer.
Add 4–5 mL of cold sorting buffer through the strainer gently to stop the enzymatic reaction and help cells pass through.
Remove and discard non-disaggregated tissue pieces from the filter.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge samples at 50 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant into a new 15 mL Falcon tube.
Discard the pellet containing mostly cardiomyocytes and cell aggregates.
Centrifuge samples at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant into a new 15 mL Falcon tube.
Discard the pellet containing mostly small cells such as fibroblasts, leukocytes, and endothelial cells.
Centrifuge samples at 1,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Keep the pellet enriched in cardiac exophers.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of sorting buffer containing antibodies at the desired concentration.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Add 1-2 mL of sorting buffer to wash off excess antibody.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and keep the pellet.
Re-suspend the pellet in 1 mL of sorting buffer containing Draq5 (1:5,000 dilution).
Keep samples at 4°C in the dark.
Prepare 1.5 mL Falcon tubes with 100 μL of collection buffer for exopher sorting if needed.
Perform flow cytometry analysis within the next 4 hours.
Use ice-cold solutions and avoid mechanical dissociation of tissue to minimize debris generation.
Use only cells or cardiac exophers disaggregated by enzymatic digestion.
Discard particles containing DNA (Draq5+).
Discard particles containing endothelial markers (CD31+).
Use the fluorescence signal from cardiomyocytes in your fluorescent reporter model to identify cardiac derived exophers.
Use wild-type or Cre-negative mice as a control to establish the gate.
Induce Tdtomato fluorescent protein expression specifically in cardiomyocytes by crossing mice with αMHCCRE with Rosa26Tdtom.
Utilize animals from 1 to 50 weeks of age and both sexes for similar results.
Back-gate detected cardiac exophers to better define your gates.
